The function $f(x)$ is defined and differentiable on $[-4,5].$ The graph of ${f}^{′}(x),$ the derivative of $f(x),$ is shown above. Given that $f(2)=-3,$ what is the minimum value ${f}_{\text{min}}$ of $f(x)$ on the interval $[-4,5]?$

{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
According to the candidates test, the minimum value of $f(x)$ on $[-4,5]$ must occur at a critical point or an endpoint of the interval. 

**Step 1**: Find the critical points:

We see that ${f}^{′}(x)$ is defined everywhere on $x\in (-4,5),$ and ${f}^{′}(x)=0$ at $x=2.$ Therefore, the candidates are $x=-4,2,5.$

**Step 2**: Compute the value of $f$ for each candidate using the fundamental theorem of calculus:

The function is made up of $2$ trapezoids. Let's add the areas bounded by these shapes to our diagram:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14243229/assets/cf8e3aa5a6000966c44b36071b2269540578cf123a19024a20a62fb61896dc51.png)

Using the given information and the fundamental theorem of calculus, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2) & =-3 \\ f(-4) & =f(2)+{\int }_{2}^{-4}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =f(2)-{\int }_{-4}^{2}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-3-(-16) \\  & =13 \\ f(5) & =f(2)+{\int }_{2}^{5}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-3+4 \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Select the smallest value of $f$ from our candidates. 

Comparing the values of $f$ found in step $2,$ we have

$$
{f}_{\text{min}}=min\{-3,13,1\}=-3.
$$

Therefore, the minimum value of $f$ is ${f}_{\text{min}}=-3,$ and the value of $x$ that minimizes $f(x)$ is ${x}_{\text{min}}=2.$
